rules.sentence: The progressive accumulation of GAG in the abdominal viscera causes hepatosplenomegaly.
One of the first clinical signs of Hunter syndrome is protruded abdomen.
Hepatosplenomegaly elevates intra-abdominal pressure, causing increased tension on the abdominal wall.
This may result in an inguinal and umbilical hernia.
Patients complain of chronic diarrhea with voluminous, mucoid stools.
Patients present with coarse facial features, short stature, joint contractures, joint stiffness, and myopathy.
The skeletal manifestations in Hunter syndrome cause a rare congenital condition known as dysostosis multiplex.
The failure of endochondral ossification due to GAG accumulation in the growth plate results in short stature.
It also results in kyphosis, scoliosis, and structural deformities in the rib cage.[10]
